question: Compare PostgreSQL 17 and PostgreSQL 18 using official release notes: which performance, developer and operational features changed, and what should a small SaaS team verify before upgrading?
title: PostgreSQL 17 vs PostgreSQL 18: Feature Comparison and Upgrade Considerations

sentences.text: PostgreSQL 18 brings major performance improvements, including an asynchronous I/O subsystem and skip-scan lookup capabilities for multicolumn B-tree indexes.
Developer-facing additions include native support for virtual generated columns, the uuidv7() function for timestamp-ordered UUID generation, and OLD and NEW aliases in RETURNING clauses.

Operationally, the release introduces notable backward incompatibilities, including changes to VACUUM and ANALYZE inheritance handling, the deprecation of MD5 password authentication, and adjustments to time zone abbreviation resolution.
PostgreSQL 18 introduces an asynchronous I/O subsystem to improve the performance of sequential scans, bitmap heap scans, and vacuums.
PostgreSQL 18 adds skip-scan lookups for multicolumn B-tree indexes, allowing queries to use indexes even when leading columns lack restrictions.
PostgreSQL 18 includes the uuidv7() function to generate timestamp-ordered UUIDs.
PostgreSQL 18 supports OLD and NEW aliases in RETURNING clauses for INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and MERGE operations.
PostgreSQL 18 adds support for virtual generated columns that compute values dynamically during read operations.
PostgreSQL 18 introduces the UNIQUE NULLS DISTINCT constraint, which treats NULL values as unique and prevents duplicate NULL entries.
PostgreSQL 18 introduces support for OAuth authentication.
According to a single source, initdb enables data checksums by default in PostgreSQL 18, and pg_upgrade requires matching cluster checksum settings.
According to a single source, VACUUM and ANALYZE process inheritance children by default unless the ONLY option is used.
According to single-source findings, MD5 password authentication is deprecated in PostgreSQL 18, with CREATE ROLE and ALTER ROLE emitting deprecation warnings.
According to a single source, users with indexes on ltree columns who do not use the libc collation provider must reindex their ltree columns after upgrading to PostgreSQL 18.2.
PostgreSQL 18 provides significant performance and developer enhancements through asynchronous I/O, skip scan, uuidv7(), and virtual generated columns.

Small SaaS teams upgrading from PostgreSQL 17 must account for operational breaking changes, particularly the deprecation of MD5 authentication, default checksum activation, and inheritance handling in maintenance tasks.

k1.statement: PostgreSQL 18 introduces an optimizer optimization that automatically removes some unnecessary table self-joins, which can be disabled via the server variable enable_self_join_elimination.

k2.statement: PostgreSQL 18 supports 'skip scan' lookups for multicolumn B-tree indexes, allowing their use in cases where there are no restrictions on the first or early indexed columns.

k3.statement: PostgreSQL 18 includes a uuidv7() function for generating timestamp-ordered UUIDs.

k4.statement: PostgreSQL 18 adds support for OLD and NEW in RETURNING clauses for INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and MERGE commands.

k5.statement: PostgreSQL 18 adds pg_stat_all_tables columns to report time spent in VACUUM, ANALYZE, and their automatic variants.

k6.statement: PostgreSQL 18 changes the initdb default to enable data checksums, which can be disabled using the new --no-data-checksums option.

k7.statement: PostgreSQL 18 deprecates MD5 password authentication, with CREATE ROLE and ALTER ROLE now emitting deprecation warnings.

k8.statement: PostgreSQL 18 introduces parallelized COPY FROM operations to speed up bulk imports by using multiple workers instead of a single thread.

k9.statement: Functions written in SQL or PL/pgSQL in PostgreSQL 18 feature improved inlining, execution plan reuse, and better integration with parallel and JIT execution.

k10.statement: PostgreSQL 18 introduces the UNIQUE NULLS DISTINCT constraint, which treats NULLs as unique values and prevents duplicate NULLs in unique constraints.

k11.statement: PostgreSQL 18 introduces full logical replication support for DDL statements such as CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, and DROP, allowing them to be automatically replicated to subscribers.

k12.statement: PostgreSQL 18 adds the pg_stat_io system view to provide native insight into read and write I/O behavior across buffers and relation types.

k13.statement: PostgreSQL 18 improves the MERGE statement with better standards compliance, refined conditional logic resolution, and improvements for WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT.

k14.statement: PostgreSQL 18 introduces skip-scan for multi-column B-tree indexes, allowing the planner to iterate over leading column distinct values to satisfy predicates on later columns when the leading column is not constrained.

k15.statement: PostgreSQL 18 defaults generated columns to be 'virtual' rather than stored.

k16.statement: PostgreSQL 18 introduces support for OAuth authentication.

k17.statement: PostgreSQL 18 enables data checksums by default for new clusters initialized with initdb.

k18.statement: PostgreSQL 18 introduces an asynchronous I/O subsystem that allows queuing multiple read requests simultaneously to improve performance for sequential scans, bitmap heap scans, and vacuums.

k19.statement: The skip scan capability allows the query planner to use multicolumn indexes even when early columns lack equality restrictions.

k20.statement: The optimizer can now automatically eliminate unnecessary self-joins.

k21.statement: Virtual generated columns are now the default behavior, computing values on read instead of storing them on write.

k22.statement: Temporal constraints for defining non-overlapping PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, and FOREIGN KEY constraints on range types are supported via the WITHOUT OVERLAPS clause.

k23.statement: The uuidv7() function is introduced for generating timestamp-ordered UUIDs.

k24.statement: The RETURNING clause now supports OLD and NEW aliases to reference pre-modification and post-modification values.

k25.statement: The pg_upgrade utility now preserves optimizer statistics during major version upgrades.

k26.statement: Native OAuth authentication support is added for validating tokens issued by OAuth providers.

k27.statement: Data checksums are enabled by default for new clusters initialized with initdb.

k28.statement: VACUUM and ANALYZE process inheritance children by default, changing from the previous behavior of processing only the parent table.

k29.statement: PostgreSQL 18 prioritizes session time zone abbreviations over server-wide settings.

k30.statement: MD5 authentication is deprecated, with warnings emitted for CREATE ROLE and ALTER ROLE commands setting MD5 passwords.

k31.statement: PostgreSQL 18 implements Self-Join Elimination (SJE), which automatically detects and removes redundant self-joins in SELECT queries when the join condition uses a unique or primary key.

k32.statement: PostgreSQL 18 includes buffer statistics in EXPLAIN ANALYZE output by default, removing the requirement to explicitly set the BUFFERS option.

k33.statement: PostgreSQL 18 exposes storage visibility for materialized nodes in query plans, reporting whether intermediate results are held in memory or spilled to disk, including peak storage consumed.

k34.statement: Self-Join Elimination is introduced, replacing redundant self-joins of a plain table with a scan.

k35.statement: Async I/O (AIO) is introduced in PostgreSQL 18, providing performance improvements for sequential scans.

k36.statement: PostgreSQL 18 adds support for VIRTUAL generated columns as the default, replacing the previous implicit behavior.

k37.statement: The RETURNING clause in PostgreSQL 18 supports OLD and NEW aliases to return data values from rows.

k38.statement: PostgreSQL 18 improves pg_upgrade by adding support for parallel jobs and transferring statistics from previous versions.

k39.statement: EXPLAIN ANALYZE defaults to include BUFFERS in PostgreSQL 18.

k40.statement: PostgreSQL 18 introduces an asynchronous I/O (AIO) subsystem to improve performance of sequential scans, bitmap heap scans, and vacuums.

k41.statement: PostgreSQL 18 supports virtual generated columns which compute values during read operations.

k42.statement: The initdb default has been changed to enable data checksums.

k43.statement: MD5 password authentication is deprecated in PostgreSQL 18.

k44.statement: VACUUM and ANALYZE process inheritance children of a parent by default, requiring the new ONLY option to revert to previous behavior.

k45.statement: PostgreSQL 18 introduces an asynchronous I/O subsystem, which can be configured via the 'io_method' server variable.

k46.statement: The new system view 'pg_aios' allows monitoring of asynchronous I/O operations.

k47.statement: The uuidv4() function is now an alias for gen_random_uuid().

k48.statement: NOT NULL constraints can now be added with the NOT VALID clause, avoiding a full table scan during creation.

k49.statement: PostgreSQL 18 includes several backward incompatibilities, including changes to time zone abbreviation handling, MD5 password deprecation, VACUUM/ANALYZE inheritance behavior, and COPY FROM end-of-file handling.

k50.statement: PostgreSQL 18 introduces an asynchronous I/O (AIO) subsystem supporting sequential scans, bitmap heap scans, and vacuum, with up to 3x performance gains in certain scenarios.

k51.statement: PostgreSQL 18 introduces an asynchronous I/O (AIO) subsystem, utilizing Linux 'io_uring' or a worker-based implementation to improve throughput and latency, with reported 2-3x performance improvements for certain operations.

k52.statement: PostgreSQL 18 adds support for skip scan lookups on multicolumn B-tree indexes.

k53.statement: PostgreSQL 18 introduces virtual generated columns as the default option, computing values just-in-time during query execution.

k54.statement: The RETURNING clause in INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and MERGE commands now allows access to both the previous (OLD) and current (NEW) values.

k55.statement: Data checksums, used to validate the integrity of stored data, are enabled by default for new clusters in PostgreSQL 18.

k56.statement: PostgreSQL 18 deprecates md5 password authentication in favor of SCRAM authentication.

k57.statement: Parallelism in hash right semi joins is disabled because of a race condition in updating the join's shared hash table.

k58.statement: A dump/restore is not required for users upgrading within the 18.X version series.

k59.statement: Generated columns are explicitly disallowed in partition keys, fixing cases where implicit column references previously bypassed checks.

k60.statement: Generated columns are disallowed in COPY FROM WHERE clauses as they have not yet been computed when the filter is applied.

k61.statement: Databases running PostgreSQL 18.2 may require reindexing of all ltree columns after updating.

k62.statement: PostgreSQL 18 introduced new string lowercasing behavior in some locales where lower-casing a string can produce more characters than the original, which impacts contrib/pg_trgm.

k63.statement: PostgreSQL 18 increased the usage of PlaceHolderVar nodes in query planning compared to previous versions.

k64.statement: PostgreSQL 18.2 escalates errors during NOTIFY message processing to FATAL, which results in closing the client connection.

k65.statement: Users with indexes on ltree columns who do not use the libc collation provider must reindex their ltree columns after upgrading to PostgreSQL 18.2.

k66.statement: PostgreSQL 18 introduces the publication parameter 'publish_generated_columns' to enable replication of stored generated columns.

k67.statement: The 'publish_generated_columns' parameter accepts two values: 'NONE' (the default) and 'STORED'.

k68.statement: Virtual generated columns cannot be replicated in PostgreSQL 18.

k69.statement: When replicating stored generated columns, the subscriber table must define the receiving column as a regular (non-generated) column; otherwise, the apply process will error.

k70.statement: PostgreSQL 18 enhances the 'pg_stat_subscription_stats' view with new columns for tracking specific replication conflict types.

k71.statement: PostgreSQL 18 adds support for virtual generated columns.

k72.statement: PostgreSQL 18 logical replication introduces fine-grained filtering and parallel streaming.

k73.statement: PostgreSQL 18 enables checksums by default for new clusters.

k74.statement: PostgreSQL 18 enables querying JSON data as if it were a normal table.
